qt: to the Commission Afroditi Latinopoulou (PfE) Subject:

The new Pact on Migration and Asylum changes the framework for responsibility-sharing between Member States. It is crucial for Member States along the external border, such as Greece, to have a clear picture regarding potential transfers of applicants for international protection to their territory from other EU Member States. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

How many transfers of applicants for international protection to Greece does it foresee in 2026 and 2027 under the new rules for determining which Member State is responsible for an asylum application?
From which Member States are these transfers expected to take place and on the basis of what criteria will the number of transfers be determined?
How will it ensure that the application of the rules on determining responsibility does not disproportionately increase the pressure on countries of first entry, in particular Greece?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.10.2026) The Commission cannot provide a forecast of the number of transfers of applicants for international protection to Greece in 2026 and 2027. This depends on a number of factors including the number of applicants registering applications in another Member States, the circumstances relevant for the application of the responsibility criteria, the existence of family links, prior residence documents or visas, illegal entry or stay, the practical implementation of the new rules by the national authorities concerned and other factors. The Commission cannot identify in advance from which Member States transfers are expected to take place. Responsibility is determined on the basis of the criteria laid down in Regulation (EU) 2024/13511. A key objective of the Pact on Migration and Asylum2 is to ensure a balance between solidarity and responsibility, avoiding placing disproportionate pressure on Member States of first entry. The new system combines rules on responsibility with a mandatory but flexible solidarity mechanism designed to support Member States under migratory pressure. In the context of the first migration management cycle under the Pact3, Greece was considered under migratory pressure and is benefitting from solidarity.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 on asylum and
